data.content_ref: inline:The problem asks for the single mechanism that BEST explains why the nocturnal UHI gap is larger in some cities than in others. SRC_001 asserts anthropogenic heat is that single dominant mechanism and demotes stored thermal-mass release to a secondary role. But on a clear, calm night, reduced turbulent mixing maximizes the influence of longwave radiative trapping and slow release of stored heat from urban materials (thermal mass/sky view), while the cross-city literature consistently finds that urban geometry (sky view factor) and thermal storage—not population density—dominate inter-city UHI differences under these specific conditions. By pinning the cross-city gap on population density and energy consumption, the target ignores the mechanism most responsible for the sustained night-time temperature difference.
